unresolved_v4_constants._note: Operator H-clarification (2026-07-23): the empirical-CDF tie convention is an explicit methodology constant, not an implementation detail — the shadow study measured a candidate sub-score difference of up to ~0.38 between weak_le and mid_rank on tie-heavy series. It lives under _meta because the loader rejects <PIN> in any score-effective path by design; on S5-v4 activation the approved value moves to indicators.s5 as a real constant.

_meta._note: methodology_frozen_at was set to 2026-07-15 by operator decision of record (2026-07-19 review): the last score-effective methodology change up to that point was v3.3.2 (commits 0d6c9a0/4bf5c53, 2026-07-15), and every version between was 'methodology unchanged'. v4.0-s4-endpoint moves it to 2026-08-22 (see below). falsification_tracking_since was never recorded in the codebase (Phase-0 audit) and remains <PIN> until a real prospective observation process exists (first persisted production snapshot + methodology hash + append-only outcome recording); it must not be backdated. Neither field is score-effective; both are excluded from the completeness gate. Every other value below is byte-faithful to the runtime literals as of service_version 3.7.8; the seeded-MC golden headline is 52.43. v4.0-s4-endpoint (2026-08-22) adds gsadf.statistic and moves methodology_frozen_at: s4 now scores the BSADF at the LAST observation against the endpoint row of the simulated BSADF CV matrix, not the GSADF sup over all endpoints. Rationale, measured with exuber 1.1.0 on CPI-deflated native Nasdaq-100 monthly log levels from 1986 (T=487): the GSADF rejects at 5 percent (2.6189 > cv95 2.2604) with the sup attained at a window ending 2000-02, while the BSADF at the 2026-07 endpoint is 0.7562 against endpoint cv90 1.1769 -- the sup reports a 26-year-old episode as a present-day regime. BOUND: gsadf.series_months_max = 360 caps every runtime fit, so T=487 is an OFFLINE measurement the service never performs; on the 360-month tail it does fit, the same series gives GSADF 1.3234 against cv95 2.2099 (no rejection, sup dated 2021-08) while the endpoint is 0.7562 under both. The sup changes its verdict with the window length it is handed; the endpoint does not. That invariance, measured at the length actually fitted, is the load-bearing argument for scoring the endpoint. v4.1-s4-asymmetric-contested (2026-08-23) adds gsadf.contested_rule = 'asymmetric' and is the first SCORE-SHIFTING change in this line -- v4.0 moved what s4 measures, this moves what it returns. Chen, Chen & Huang (2026) establish SIZE distortion: PSY over-rejects under hump-shaped GPT fundamentals, which bounds FALSE POSITIVES and says nothing against a non-rejection. A test biased toward rejecting that still fails to reject is stronger evidence of no explosiveness, not weaker, so capping that reading at 0.25 discarded the one result the critique gives most reason to trust -- and at the live statistic 0.25 sits ABOVE what the test returned (SUB_NULL 0.05), so the 'conservative cap' was a floor pushing the headline UP. Under 'asymmetric' a REJECTION is still capped, because that is where the critique bites; only the non-rejection passes through. Measured effect: s4 0.25 -> 0.05, headline 53.30 -> 51.82, delta -1.48, action band UNCHANGED at 'trim'. THE MARGIN IS THIN, AND ON THE SCORED INSTRUMENT, NOT THE SHADOW. The scored path is NOMINAL (compute.py fetches the QQQ proxy and takes logs; no deflation); the CPI-deflated series is the shadow, reported and never scored. On the nominal T=331 series the endpoint BSADF is 1.1315 against endpoint cv90 1.1393 -- a non-rejection by 0.0078, i.e. 0.7 percent of the critical value. The deflated shadow reads 0.7562 against the same 1.1393, a 34 percent margin; an earlier draft of this note recorded THAT as the live reading and so implied a comfort the scored instrument does not have. Under the old symmetric rule this distance was inert (0.25 on either side). v4.1 makes it the entire pivot: one ordinary data revision can move 1.48 headline points.  The golden headline stays 52.43 because the golden fixture supplies no GSADF input, so s4 floors there under either rule -- that is a property of the fixture, not evidence the change is score-neutral; it is not. RESIDUAL, STATED, AND IT IS LARGER THAN A CAVEAT. (1) Chen et al. measure the PSY procedure, which is a SUPREMUM over endpoints. Since v4.0 s4 scores a SINGLE endpoint. Over-rejection of a sup does not imply over-rejection at a fixed endpoint -- much of a sup's spurious size is multiplicity across endpoints, and this repo's own measurements put the sup's mass mid-sample (argmax 2000-02 at T=487, 2021-08 at T=360), not at the endpoint. So endpoint-level size distortion is ASSUMED HERE, NOT SHOWN, and it is the premise the release rests on. (2) The endpoint BSADF is the least powerful member of the family, one term of the sup, so LOW POWER is not a generic caveat but the leading alternative explanation for a non-rejection. (3) Chen et al. run detrended log prices (93 percent) and the price-dividend ratio (100 percent); s4 runs raw log prices, neither, so those figures bound the concern rather than measure this configuration. SUB_NULL is 'tested and not explosive', never 'certainly calm'. The golden headline is UNCHANGED at 52.43, though note what that does and does not show: the golden fixture supplies no GSADF input at all, so s4 floors there whichever statistic is selected. As of v4.1 that cap no longer binds a non-rejection, so at current data neither statistic scores 0.25; the v4.0 sub-score claim below is stated as it was true at v4.0 and is superseded here. IndicatorOutput('s4').value, the rf1 record built by persist_snapshot and the dashboard feed's metrics.gsadf all now carry the endpoint statistic where they carried the sup.
